row.evidence: SproutVideo's help centre has no SCIM or provisioning article; team members are added with "+ ADD A TEAM MEMBER" and removed with the trash can icon, and its SSO only redirects video-website visitors to the customer's IdP.
row.notes: No SCIM by absence (pricing page, full help-centre sitemap and API reference searched). Flat plans with seat counts: Seed $12/mo (2 seats), Sprout $35 (5), Tree $72 (10), Forest $195 (50+), all billed annually, so per-user fields are null. SAML SSO on Forest is for video-website viewers, not team-member login, so sso_plan is null. The REST API covers videos, playlists and viewer logins, not team members. Okta OIN app is SWA only.

plans.name: Forest
plans.notes: Forest adds SAML SSO for video-website viewers, not for team-member sign-in. sso=false refers to team-member sign-in; scim/user_api false because no SCIM or team-member API is documented on any plan.

scim.notes: No SCIM endpoint is documented. Team members are invited and removed by hand in Account Settings > Team Members. The SSO feature authenticates viewers of SproutVideo video websites, not team members.

limitations.text: Viewer logins in the API grant access to specific videos and cannot sign in to the account.

user_api.notes: The REST API manages videos, tags, playlists, folders, live streams and viewer logins/access grants; it has no team-member (account user) endpoints.

okta.notes: OIN app is SWA (password vaulting) only. Okta also hosts a SAML setup doc for SproutVideo video-website viewer SSO.

google.notes: Google is used as a custom SAML app for video-website viewer SSO, not a catalogue app.

searched: https://sproutvideo.com/sitemap.xml (all 230+ help articles fetched and grepped for scim, provisioning, saml, okta, azure, single sign)
open_questions: Docs do not say whether team members can sign in to the SproutVideo account with SAML SSO; only viewer SSO for video websites is documented.
Which plans include the API and the Account Audit Log is not stated in text (pricing table uses icons; the audit-log article says 'certain plans').
